title: President Lai Promulgates Act on Strengthening Defense Autonomy and Developing the Unmanned Vehicles Industry
detail: President William Lai promulgated the "Act on Strengthening Defense Autonomy and Developing the Unmanned Vehicles Industry" on September 11, 2026, after Premier Cho Jung-tai countersigned it, resolving the drone-funding standoff that began August 27 when the opposition-controlled Legislative Yuan rejected the Cabinet's NT$210 billion special drone budget and passed its own KMT/TPP-authored bill instead. The act allocates NT$240 billion (~US$7.61 billion) over six years — roughly NT$40 billion annually, with room for additional legislature-approved funding — for domestically produced 'low-cost, high-performance' unmanned systems, designating the Ministry of Economic Affairs as lead authority while the Ministry of National Defense oversees military procurement. The budget provision took immediate effect; other provisions take effect in six months. Presidential Office Deputy Secretary-General Xavier Chang said the government would 'use national demand to create markets, use markets to support research and development' and 'use industrial strength to bolster national defense.' DPP caucus secretary-general Fan Yun said promulgation 'would reinforce international confidence in the feasibility of developing non-China supply chains in Taiwan,' while KMT's Chen I-hsin said the opposition's version 'provides greater resources and flexibility' than the Executive Yuan's original proposal. Defense Minister Wellington Koo had previously warned the NT$40 billion annual cap is insufficient against MND's own NT$42.1 billion drone-procurement plan.
